absent: Actual interrupt dispatch, flow handling, threading, resend execution and statistics reporting beyond initialization and teardown shown.
Descriptor lookup, concurrent map access rules, reference counting transitions and final memory reclamation after the deferred free is scheduled.
Proc, sysfs and debugfs content, permissions and show or store behavior beyond entry creation and removal.
Domain address translation, mapping, association, parent hierarchy locking and publish or lookup ordering.
Generic chip register access, mask and acknowledge behavior and nested lock usage beyond assignment.
Device resource lifetime, rollback on probe failure and error injection beyond the wrappers shown.
Architecture specific lower bound policy, NUMA node choice and default affinity construction.

findings.text: Allocation service accepts either a fixed number with a lower bound or a free search hint, validates the request size, enforces architecture lower bound for dynamic numbers, and returns the start of the reserved range or a negative failure indication.
Device bound allocation wrapper reserves a descriptor range and records base and count for automatic release on device detach, forwarding failures from the core allocator without recording.
Domain lifecycle interface creates and publishes a domain from an info bundle, removes a domain with cleanup of generic chips and default pointer, and allows setting the global default domain.

Generic chip services initialize a chip container, attach a masked subset of lines with chip handling and status adjustments, detach lines back to safe defaults, and allocate per domain chip arrays with cleanup on failure.
Descriptor release entry defers final freeing through read copy update so that demultiplexing readers and statistics readers can proceed without exclusive locking.
Proc teardown entry removes affinity related nodes, spurious node and numeric node when both global and per descriptor directories exist, otherwise it does nothing.
Fresh descriptors are inert by construction with safe fallback handling, disabled and masked status, neutral linkage, zeroed accounting, single ownership reference and default affinity.
Presence in sysfs is tracked by a dedicated istate bit set only after successful addition and checked before deletion, so early boot or failed addition never deletes, and addition failure only warns.

Affinity handling falls back to a global default when none is supplied, copies the effective mask, clears pending state where applicable, retains node choice where applicable, and marks managed descriptors with dedicated indications and node derived from the mask.

Domain creation enforces consistent mapping options and establishes firmware linkage, operation and host context, bus and capacity limits, revmap storage, naming and root locking before hierarchy validation.

Domain naming prefers firmware chip names with bus qualification, then firmware node names with optional suffix, then an unknown fallback, rejecting suffix use with firmware chip nodes and reporting invalid firmware types.
Mask cache initialization directs each chip type at either a shared cache or its private cache and optionally preloads cached values from hardware depending on supplied flags.
Proc numeric width is derived from total descriptor capacity by decimal magnitude and is only ever raised under protection, never lowered.
Total descriptor capacity only grows through bounded expansion that recalculates proc width, with out of range requests failing without changing capacity.

Several helpers have build dependent empty forms that do nothing, covering sysfs, mask allocation, multiprocessing init, resend init, proc precision, generic chip init, debugfs removal, capacity expansion in non sparse builds, proc unregistration and reference release.
A global mutex serializes free area search, capacity expansion and descriptor insertion for allocation so concurrent allocators cannot claim overlapping ranges.
Descriptor reset to defaults during freeing holds the per descriptor raw spinlock with interrupt save, while statistics clearing and map erasure occur outside that critical section.
A global raw spinlock protects the generic chip list during addition and removal, with interrupt save used in the domain chip allocation path.

Domain removal holds the domain mutex while detaching debug state, list linkage and default pointer, proc width update holds its raw spinlock with interrupt save, and descriptor creation initializes its raw spinlock with a dedicated class plus a request mutex and thread wait queue.
Device managed generic chip record holds a chip pointer, a bit mask of lines, and clear and set status adjustments applied on release.

Descriptor storage includes per cpu statistics, affinity and pending masks, raw lock, request mutex, thread wait queue, common and per irq data, resend linkage, and in sparse builds a kernel object and read copy update head.

Domain storage includes firmware reference, operation table, host data, bus token, hardware limits, revmap size, revmap tree, name, flags, exit hook, device pointer, parent and root links, mutex and optional generic chip container.

Generic chip container holds a lock, type count, hardware or virtual base, register base, named chip types with shared handler, domain link, big endian accessors when flagged and a computed line count.

Range lifecycle moves from free area search to capacity assurance to per number allocation and insertion with sysfs and debug registration, with any per number failure rolling back previously inserted numbers in reverse order.

Single descriptor lifecycle moves from zeroed allocation through statistics and mask allocation and lock initialization to defaults and object init, while freeing resets defaults, clears statistics and erases the map entry, with final memory release deferred via read copy update.

Domain lifecycle moves from creation through flag assignment, parent linkage, chip allocation, custom init and publication to optional descriptor instantiation and association, with init or chip failures unwinding chips and freeing the domain, while removal runs exit, detaches, destroys chips when flagged and frees.

Line attach adds the container to the global list once, initializes mask caches, then per set bit optionally assigns nested lock classes, computes a per line mask, binds chip with handler and chip data and adjusts status, while detach removes the container once then per set bit clears handler, chip, data and adjusts status, resolving virtual numbers through the domain when present.

Allocation fails without side effects on zero count, fixed number below the start hint, empty affinity mask, missing free area, fixed number mismatch, capacity beyond sparse maximum and memory exhaustion during descriptor or mask allocation.

Domain paths warn on inconsistent mapping options, reject busy chip container reuse and zero chip counts, propagate custom init failures with chip teardown and warn if the reverse map is non empty at removal.

Allocation and creation report invalid argument for bad sizes and masks, already exists for fixed number collision, no space for missing free area, no memory for allocation failures and busy for duplicate chip containers.
Fresh descriptors use depth one and reference count one with disabled and masked indications and default init flags, while sysfs presence uses a dedicated istate bit.
In the non sparse variant allocation over a range only assigns owner and inserts the preexisting descriptors, returning the start without affinity validation or rollback.
Domain destruction releases the firmware reference, marks it uninitialized, frees the name only when it was dynamically allocated, then frees the container.
Debug filesystem teardown for a domain removes the entry named by the domain under the global domain directory in the enabled build and does nothing otherwise.
